Defaults of the tumour mode

Source: R/clones_tumour.R
clone_defaults.Rd

Discovery: classes, depth_delta, cap, min_n, disc_allele, test_allele, n_pc, k, max_leaves, min_size, q, n_perm, drift_test, max_cells, split_depth (discovery / test halves of the window depth as well as of the votes). Merge / split tests (merge_clones(), discover_within(), the split pass; perm_decision): "quantile" (default) = the observed contrast above the type-7 q-quantile of n_perm permutations (with 200 permutations at q = 0.999 this is "beats about the maximum": ~6 false splits per 1,000 tests of one clone, not 1); "pvalue" = permutation p-value (1 + #null >= observed) / (1 + permutations) <= 1 - q, over max(n_perm, ceiling(1 / (1 - q)) - 1) permutations (999 at q = 0.999) with an exact early stop for "same" (as soon as p can no longer reach 1 - q); a "different" verdict runs every permutation. The run notes give the number of tests and the expected false splits n_tests x (1 - q).

Usage

clone_defaults()

Value

named list (see caller_tumour())

Details

Allele scale of discovery and tests (coverage-free by default since the development version): disc_allele = the allelic columns of the discovery feature matrices (clone_feature_matrix(), discover_within()); test_allele = the per-cell allele values of the merge / split contrast. "z" (the default up to 0.1.1) = the standardised count (nA - n / 2) / sd(n), whose expectation in an imbalanced region grows like (f - 0.5) sqrt(n): deep and shallow cells of one clone form separate leaves and test different. "fraction" (default of disc_allele) = the cell's oriented fraction nA / n, whose expectation does not depend on the cell's depth (discovery: in units of the null SD at the region's median vote count, the same scale as "z" for a typical cell; a cell below min_n votes gets the region's mean instead of 0; the regions of discover_within() are still selected on "z"); test_allele = "centred" (default) = the standardised count about the compared cells' pooled fraction instead of 1 / 2 (mean 0 at any depth when the two sets share the fraction; weights the cells like "z"). The imbalance term of the contrast (depth support) always uses "z".

Drift-aware split test (drift_test, default "modes_event"): the discovery and test halves of the votes are thinned from the same molecules, so a cell-level drift of the haplotype share beyond binomial noise is in both: leaves that discovery cut along the drift of one clone differ on the test half too, and the permutation null of random splits does not model that selection. "none" (the default up to 0.1.1) = the permutation contrast decides. "modes" = a pair the contrast calls different stays different when a depth term alone beats the null threshold (the drift is allelic); an allele-driven difference must in addition be discrete on at least one of the (up to 3) regions whose allele term alone beats the threshold: the per-cell oriented fractions there of the population under discovery (all leaf cells of the merge: the discovery cells, or a trunk's deep cells; the clone itself in the split pass; test half, phase blocks oriented leave-one-out by the population, cells with >= 10 votes, at most 1,500 cells) are multimodal by Silverman's critical bandwidth test (smoothed bootstrap, 199 draws, level 0.01; a continuous drift, also a skewed one, has one mode, a subclone adds one), and the two clones lie on different sides of the antimode (their fractions above it differ by >= 0.5). The population, not the union of the two clones, is tested because two leaves cut from one continuum can make a union with two modes. A subclone whose allelic difference is smaller than the drift has no mode of its own and is merged. The tests tables gain differ_contrast (the contrast's verdict), by_depth, discrete, mode_p, mode_sep. "modes_event" (default) = "modes", and a pair also stays different when the events of one set are absent from the other: the other set is allelically balanced (oriented by its own other half, |t| <= 2) on at least 75 % of the chromosomes, and on at least 2 of them, where the first set is imbalanced beyond the null threshold (two lineages), or the other set has no imbalanced region at all and is balanced on one of them (normal cells against cells with an event; column by_event). A cut along a drift of one clone can bring a set to 1/2 on one arm, not on most of the other set's events on independent chromosomes, nor make it event-free. With "modes", a group of normal cells with some tumour cells can merge with the normal cells (allele-only difference, no mode of its own), and the merged clone, which carries weak events, is then not replaced by the normal clone N0 (no reference pool).

Hierarchy: trunks = average-linkage groups of clone_allelic_distance() cut at trunk_dist (bp x haplotype fraction; e.g. 100 Mb differing by 0.3); trunk cells = trunk posterior >= trunk_post; discover_within() with disp_min, imb_min, deep_q, depth_w, max_leaves_trunk, n_nb_trunk; final split pass after the EM rounds (split_pass): FALSE (default) or "disagree" = split_disagree() (opt-in: members whose own segment state disagrees with the clone state; split_sep, split_max splits per pass, split_cand candidates tested per clone, split_min_len minimal segment length, split_min_df major-fraction step of an alternative between amplified states, see split_alt_states(), split_min_excess minimal contradiction above its noise floor). Normal hypothesis (normal_hypothesis): a fixed all-neutral clone N0 replaces every fitted clone without a non-neutral segment >= normal_min_event bp in each round. States: size_small, small_clone, p_switch, min_win, min_llr; segment rules of segment_clone() (all segmentations of the run, including the split pass): min_excess (pooled allelic excess of imbalanced runs), max_contra (gains / losses contradicted by depth become copy-neutral), bal_frac and min_bal_len (support of balanced 2:2 runs), gain_support (an imbalanced gain needs this share of its expected depth shift against the region's offset, else CN-LOH or label "imbalance" with depth_ok FALSE; default 0.3, 0 = off). Clone baseline (ploidy): "fit" (default) fits per clone the copy number of its median depth (the baseline B: 3 for a near-triploid clone) from depth and alleles together (fit_clone_states() baseline = "fit"), so the states are absolute copy numbers; a number in [1, 8] fixes B for every clone; 2 is the diploid baseline of 0.1.x (a near-triploid or whole-genome-doubled clone is then fitted on a compressed scale: 2:2 as 1:1, 2:0 as 1:0). ploidy_tol (log-likelihood per window, finite, >= 0) is the tolerance within which a baseline of half the best one (a whole-genome doubling of the same profile) is preferred. Labels stay relative to the diploid normal (2:1 is a gain at any baseline, 1:1 neutral), so a clone with a baseline above 2 has non-neutral segments, and per-cell calls, over most of its genome. clones reports baseline and ploidy (the mean autosomal copy number); the run notes list the fitted baselines and name every clone whose depth contrast c sits at the lower bound of its grid (its states can be off by one copy). Assignment: mix_prior, mix_w, mix_margin, mix_rel, mix_min_dist (mixture hypotheses only for clone pairs whose states differ allelically on >= this many bp), max_mix_prior, min_post (confident), member_post (pseudobulk members), em_rounds, same_dist (clones whose states differ on < this many bp within a trunk are merged after each round). same_post = the membership posterior of assign_cells() that min_post and member_post cut: "clone" (the default up to 0.1.1) = the best clone's posterior; "group" (default) = summed over the clones of the best clone's trunk whose states differ on < same_dist bp (the clones the same-state merge joins; assignments gains post_clone, the single clone's posterior). Two clones with the same states otherwise share each cell's posterior, few cells reach member_post, both can fall below min_size and be dropped before the merge, and their cells end in another clone (e.g. the normal clone). Reference: ref_post, min_ref. Other: doublet_delta, multiplet_prob (cells above it are excluded from discovery and pseudobulks), control_min_len, repass, allelic_exclude.

checkpoint (resume cache, "" = off): an .rds path. When the file does not exist the global discovery (leaves, merged clones) and the first EM round (with the candidate baselines of ploidy = "fit" as that round left them, and its run notes) are saved there; when it exists they are read from it and the run continues from the within-trunk discovery with the same results as the run that wrote it (useful when rerunning the later steps on a large sample). The cache is not keyed: reuse it only with the same features, seed and options.

Confirmation null (per-cell confirmed calls, after assignment; assignment itself always uses the input fits): ref_null = "none" (the input rho / depth t of feat$null_fit) or "rho" (opt-in: beta-binomial rho refitted on the clean reference pool's piece votes as the confirmation scores them, oriented leave-one-out by a clone pseudobulk; the call_scn recipe on the pool's feature votes is kept as null_fit$rho_pool_features); needs >= min_ref pool cells. The depth t of the confirmation is always the input one (null_fit$tpar_confirm = null_fit$tpar; depth_t_confirm rows of null_fit.tsv); only rho can be refitted. confirm_null = "generic" (null rows scored as the best of the tumour state set, one threshold per stratum) or "matched" (each clone hypothesis clone | label | shift | f scored on the null rows oriented by that clone's pseudobulk under the same two-state set as the cells; one threshold per hypothesis x stratum, hypothesis-wide below min_null_rows; held-out fold-CV false-confirmation rates per hypothesis in null_fit$confirm_null; the default). The refitted value is null_fit$rho_confirm. confirm_sided = the allele term of the confirmation scores, cells and null rows alike (score_cells() sided): "two" (default; a cell whose opposite homologue is imbalanced also scores high) or "one" (the votes are oriented by the clone's pseudobulk, so only the clone's major haplotype counts). The fallback without null rows (type-7 quantile of cell_state_scores()) is always one-sided.

A key that is not one of these defaults stops caller_tumour() with an error, and so does a value outside its range: q, p_switch, trunk_post, min_post, ref_post, max_mix_prior and every mix_w strictly between 0 and 1, mix_prior in [0, 1), multiplet_prob, deep_q and member_post in [0, 1], counts (em_rounds, min_size, n_perm, min_win, min_ref, ...) whole numbers >= 1, the caps max_cells, max_leaves and max_leaves_trunk whole numbers >= 1 or Inf (no cap), small_clone a whole number >= 0, trunk_dist and control_min_len >= 0, the other sizes / lengths > 0, the other tolerances >= 0.
